$comment: What `coai-mcp --setup-clients` / `--install` knows about each client's MCP configuration, as MEASURED in a scratch HOME (v2 E3.S6). A client is written only when this says measured; agy stays `unmeasured` until the Windows half is measured too (the spec's measurement is Linux AND Windows). Facts are observed behaviour of the versions named, not documentation.

claude.writeWith: claude mcp add-json --scope user coai -  (JSON on stdin); claude mcp remove --scope user coai
notes: an existing name makes add-json exit 1 and change nothing, so an update is remove + add-json
a malformed file makes it exit 1, leave the file unchanged and write a .corrupted copy
`claude mcp get` and `claude mcp list` START the server for a health check: never called in product code

codex.writeWith: codex mcp add [--env K=V]... coai -- <command> [args]; codex mcp remove coai
notes: add REPLACES an existing entry: its old env and startup_timeout_sec are lost, so an update passes the old env again
a rewrite dropped an inline comment on another server's line
malformed TOML makes it exit 1 and leave the file unchanged
it warns on stderr for a HOME under /tmp: only stdout is read

agy.reason: measured on Linux only; the Windows repeat of the spec's measurement has not been run, so the installer writes nothing for agy

linux.writeWith: agy mcp add [--env K=V]... <name> <command> [args]  (flags BEFORE the name; `--` before a command that starts with `-`); agy mcp remove <name>
linux.scratchHomeStart: an empty HOME has no .gemini folder; the first add creates ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json (mode 0644) and the folders

observed.case: second add, another path, same name
observed.result: the entry is REPLACED (command changed); `Add or update`

observed.case: re-add without --env after an add with --env
observed.result: env is gone: the whole entry is replaced, like codex

observed.case: foreign entry with env, args and an unknown key present
observed.result: preserved by value; the FILE is re-serialised: keys sorted alphabetically, 2-space indent, `<` and `>` written as \u003c \u003e
file unchanged; `Error: failed to parse <file>: failed to parse JSON config`; `agy mcp list` exits 1 too

observed.case: valid JSON that is not an object ([1,2])

observed.result: treated as empty: the object is written
`MCP server not found`; file stays 0 bytes
`Error: MCP server not found`; file unchanged

observed.case: remove with no file, no folder
